title: Restaurants
description: Eating out in Korea: getting a table, ordering, spice and allergies, paying, takeout and cafés.

items.english: How many are in your party?
items.note: 분 is the honorific counter for people; answer with 명.
distractors: What would you like to order?
How many dishes would you like?
Would you like to make a reservation?

items.english: Please take a seat over here.

good.english: How long do I have to wait?

items.english: Do you have a window seat?
distractors: Do you have a private room?
Can I sit by the door?

items.english: Could I have the menu, please?
distractors: Could I have the bill, please?
Could I have some water, please?
Could I have a spoon, please?

items.english: What would you like to eat?
distractors: What would you like to drink?

good.english: Just a moment, I'll order a bit later.

items.english: Two servings of pork belly, please.
items.note: Barbecue is ordered by the serving (인분), usually two minimum.
distractors: Three servings of pork belly, please.
One serving of pork belly, please.

distractors: Please add a bottle of soju.

items.note: Side dish refills are usually free.

items.english: Could we have some small plates?
items.note: 앞접시: small individual plates for sharing dishes.

distractors: One more pair of chopsticks, please.

items.english: What would you like to drink?
distractors: What would you like to eat?
Your food will be ready soon.

items.english: Is the food to your liking?

distractors: Would you like to pay now?

items.english: This one is on the house.
items.note: 서비스 in a restaurant means something given free.

good.english: Really? Thank you, I'll enjoy it.
No, I'd like to eat a bit more.

items.english: That comes to thirty thousand won.
distractors: That comes to three thousand won.

distractors: Will you be paying in cash?

distractors: Will you pay by card or cash?
